pr_title: Add User-Agent to AzureBlob backend requests

issue_context.title: Azure Blob useragent enhancement
issue_context.body:
## Environment info
- **Duplicati version**: Latest
- **Operating system**: All
- **Backend**: Azure Blob

## Description
Please add custom user-agent string to AzureBlob connector. 

Please try hooking the user agent into the operation context sending request event as below to prepend to the existing value of the library:

```
OperationContext.GlobalSendingRequest += (sender, args) =>
    {
        string userAgent = <your user agent> + " " + Microsoft.WindowsAzure.Storage.Shared.Protocol.Constants.HeaderConstants.UserAgent;                
                args.Request.UserAgent = userAgent;
    };
```

Or if using latest SDK, hook into CustomUserAgent property: [OperationContext.CustomUserAgent Property ](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/microsoft.windowsazure.storage.operationcontext.customuseragent?view=azure-dotnet#Microsoft_WindowsAzure_Storage_OperationContext_CustomUserAgent)

If possible, please align to the format: APN/1.0 {Product Name}/{Product Version} {Feature Name}/{Feature Version}
e.g. APN/1.0 Duplicati/2.0 AzureBlob/2.0

review_comments: I wouldn't put in a hard coded string like this, rather a constant. You could add a property to the class for setting this. Also if we want to supply a user agent to services (is this the only place we do it), so that services can see what program is being used (whether this is a good thing I will leave out of the discussion), it could be a global setting for consistency.

In other places I have used the library's version:
https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/blob/master/Duplicati/Library/Backend/WEBDAV/WEBDAV.cs#L371

> I wouldn't put in a hard coded string like this, rather a constant. You could add a property to the class for setting this.

I agree

> Also if we want to supply a user agent to services (is this the only place we do it), so that services can see what program is being used, it could be a global setting for consistency.

That is a good idea indeed.

> Whether this is a good thing I will leave out of the discussion

From what I recall:

- Pros: The services can use this to better understand the use case for their servers and possibly improve as a whole or for this scenario. Or they might not care at all.
- Cons: The service could target our users? I don't know, either way, with a opt-out option this would be mitigated.

> In other places I have used the library's version: https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/blob/master/Duplicati/Library/Backend/WEBDAV/WEBDAV.cs#L371

What about using `APN/1.0 Duplicati/2.0 AzureBlob/<AssemblyVersion>`. This way we get the Duplicati base version along with the specific version of the product.

> Cons: The service could target our users? I don't know, either way, with a opt-out option this would be mitigated.

Should that happen, we can discuss the appropriate action. Generally, a service acting on the User-Agent header is asking for trouble, but it is a nice option for service debugging, stats and customer support (i.e. "the software you are using has a know issue, please upgrade").

If a provider wants to block Duplicati requests, I don't think we should play cat-and-mouse with them. Their users should complain or change providers.
@mikaelmello  I can make the change if you prefer?
